questions.q: What distinguishes semantic search from keyword search?
options: It finds documents containing the exact query words only
It never uses vectors
It finds documents that match the meaning of the query, even when the words differ
It only works on numeric data
questions.explain: Semantic search compares embeddings, so paraphrases can match even without shared words.

questions.q: Which is the correct order of a basic semantic search pipeline?
options: Embed the query, chunk the documents, retrieve, index
Chunk and embed the documents with one model, embed the query with the same model, then retrieve the top k
Retrieve, chunk, embed, train
Train a new model for every query, then chunk
questions.explain: Documents are chunked, embedded, and indexed once; each query is embedded with the same model and used to retrieve the nearest chunks.

questions.q: In the demo, why did both keyword and semantic search fail on the query "reimbursement"?
options: The word was not in the 15-ticket vocabulary, so the TF-IDF and SVD embedding could not represent it
Cosine similarity cannot handle single words
The query was too long
Semantic search only works on billing topics
questions.explain: The tiny embedding only knows words it saw while fitting. Pretrained sentence models handle unseen words and paraphrases much better.

questions.q: What does precision@3 measure for a query?
options: The time taken to return three results
The number of documents in the index divided by three
How many dimensions the embedding has
The fraction of the top 3 results that are relevant (correct topic)
questions.explain: Precision@k is the share of the top k results that are relevant. A query returning nothing scores 0.

questions.q: The demo found mean precision@3 of 0.74 (keyword) versus 0.81 (semantic) over nine queries. What is the fair conclusion?
options: Semantic search is proven better in all cases
It is a small illustrative test; a real evaluation needs many more queries judged by domain experts
Keyword search should be removed from all systems
Precision@3 cannot be computed on text
questions.explain: Nine queries is too few to conclude much. Larger, carefully labeled query sets are needed, and hybrid search often keeps the strengths of both.
